alternative: Rely on the GC for memory and keep ownership in the API contract: return and close exactly what you own (io.Closer with defer, made idempotent with sync.Once), hold non-owning edges with the weak package, and register only best-effort release with runtime.AddCleanup - do not hand-roll reference counts or owning wrappers.
idiom_name: none - GC owns memory; weak.Pointer + runtime.AddCleanup cover non-owning edges and best-effort cleanup
implementation_notes: Go pointers carry no ownership information and the language has no destructors, so the classic structure - a handle whose scope exit destroys the object - has nothing to attach to. runtime.SetFinalizer, and the newer runtime.AddCleanup that new code should prefer, run at an unspecified time and only once the object is unreachable, which makes them a safety net rather than a release contract. What replaces the structure: the GC for memory; weak.Pointer (Go 1.24) for caches and back-references that must not keep their targets alive; AddCleanup for best-effort release of attached resources; and explicit Close() plus defer for anything with a deadline or an external resource. Ownership is a documented convention about who calls Close, not a type property.
code_sketch:
func Open(addr string) (session *Session, err error)   // caller owns *Session
func (s *Session) Close() error                        // must be idempotent

s, err := Open(addr); if err != nil { return err }
defer s.Close()                                        // runs on every return path

var cache weak.Pointer[Session]                        // non-owning edge
if p := cache.Value(); p != nil { use(*p) }            // may be nil at any time
pitfalls: AddCleanup and SetFinalizer may never run (for example at program exit) and run concurrently with the program: a cleanup must not touch state that may already be gone, and must not be the only release path.
A cleanup function that captures the object it is registered for keeps that object reachable, so the cleanup never runs.
A weak.Pointer nil-check races with collection between Value() and use; copy what you need immediately and tolerate the nil result.
Two goroutines sharing one *T may both close the underlying resource; Close must be idempotent (sync.Once) because the language enforces no ownership.
